contributions.headingText: Indolent T-cell lymphoma of the GI tract (iTCL-GI) is a clonal T-cell proliferation characterized by the infiltration of the lamina propria by small mature lymphocytes lacking significant epitheliotropism and typically a protracted clinical course.
97020/1 Indolent T-cell lymphoma of gastrointestinal tract
2B2Y & XH0B02 Indolent T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of gastrointestinal tract
Acceptable: indolent T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract; indolent clonal T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract.

Most patients present with disease affecting the small intestine or colon {24009234;23861889;29592893;31558678;24316103}. However, any site in the GI tract can be involved, including the oral cavity and the oesophagus {8826934}. Dissemination to extragastrointestinal locations (e.g. bone marrow, tonsil, peripheral blood) is uncommon at diagnosis {31558678} but can occur at disease progression or transformation {10517900;24316103;23861889;29986618}.

Presenting symptoms include chronic diarrhoea, abdominal pain, vomiting, dyspepsia, and weight loss, mimicking inflammatory intestinal diseases (e.g. coeliac disease and inflammatory bowel disease) {24009234;10517900;23861889;31558678;24316103;36472661}. Peripheral lymphadenopathy is absent, but mesenteric lymphadenopathy may be observed {27353398;23861889;31558678;24316103}.

iTCL-GI is an uncommon disease with a wide geographical distribution. It arises in adulthood (median ages: 51 years and 45 years for CD4+ and CD8+ diseases, respectively), more frequently in men than in women (M:F ratio: 1.5–2:1), and rarely in adolescents {27353398;36472661}.

The etiology is unknown. Some patients have a history of inflammatory bowel disease or intestinal immune disorders {24009234;24316103;31558678}, but the relationship of these disorders with iTCL-GI is unclear.

Clonal TRB and/or TRG rearrangements are detected in all cases {24009234;23861889;29592893;31558678}. Non-recurrent DNA copy-number variants have been reported in many CD4+ cases {23861889;24316103}. However, mutations and structural variants appear to differ in distinct immunophenotypic subsets {31558678;29592893}. JAK/STAT pathway gene alterations, as well as mutations in epigenetic modifier genes (e.g. TET2, KMT2D), are present in CD4+, CD4+/CD8+, and CD4−/CD8− disorders, with CD4+ cases displaying recurrent STAT3::JAK2 fusions; whereas some CD8+ cases have been shown to harbour structural alterations involving the 3′ untranslated region of IL2 {29592893;31558678;36472661}. The mutation profiles remain stable over long periods, and accrual of mutations may presage disease progression or transformation.

The mucosa of affected sites can be thickened, with prominent folds, nodules, fissures, or ulcers {8826934;27353398}. In some cases, the infiltrate produces intestinal polyps resembling lymphomatous polyposis {8780585;15046193}.

The lamina propria is usually expanded by a dense, non-destructive infiltrate of small lymphocytes; some biopsies show only patchy involvement {27353398}. Infiltration of the muscularis mucosae and submucosa is seen at times. In small intestinal disease, the villous architecture is generally preserved, but crypt hyperplasia is not uncommon {31558678}. Intraepithelial lymphocytes are not increased in most cases; however, epithelial infiltration of the crypts or lower portions of the villi may be present {23861889;31558678;27353398}. The lymphocytes have round, ovoid, or slightly irregular nuclei; fine chromatin; indistinct nucleoli; and scant or moderate cytoplasm {27353398}. Rare admixed chronic inflammatory cells and occasional lymphoid aggregates are seen {27353398}. Epithelioid granulomas, similar to those observed in Crohn disease, can be focally present {24009234;10517900;23861889}.

Immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridization

The lymphocytes exhibit a mature T-cell phenotype. All cases express CD3, but downregulation/loss of CD5 or CD7 can be seen in a subset {27353398}. CD4+ cases appear more common than CD8+ cases {10517900;23861889;24316103;29592893;24009234;31558678}, and some might display CD4+/CD8+ or CD4−/CD8− immunophenotypes {31558678;29592893;24009234}. CD4+ cases do not express FOXP3 or PD1 {23861889}, and the CD8+ cases are TIA1+, but granzyme B expression is infrequent {24009234;31558678}. All published cases have documented TCRαβ expression. A small subset of cases is CD103+ and, rarely, CD20 {30342536}; focal/weak CD56 {8780585;24316103;31558678} expression may be observed. CD30 is negative, except in transformed lymphomas {23861889}. The neoplastic cells are negative for EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER). The Ki-67 proliferation index is extremely low (< 10%).

Differential diagnosis

Although iTCL-GI might resemble inflammatory intestinal diseases clinically, the presence of a relatively dense infiltrate of small mature lymphocytes in the lamina propria, sparse chronic inflammation, and dominant expression of CD4 or CD8, are supportive of iTCL-GI. The cytological attributes of indolent NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the GI tract (medium-sized cells, irregular nuclei, and pale pink cytoplasm) differ from those of iTCL-GI. Among primary aggressive intestinal T-cell lymphomas, monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma can show overlapping morphological and immunophenotypic features with CD8+ iTCL-GI; however, an absence of epitheliotropism and CD56 expression and a low Ki-67 proliferation index can aid in excluding monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma (see #49464Table 12.03). Secondary gastrointestinal involvement by peripheral or cutaneous T-cell lymphomas should be ruled out by clinical examination and imaging studies before diagnosing iTCL-GI.
In selected circumstances, demonstration of clonal TR rearrangement (or somatic mutations) can assist in the distinction from an inflammatory disorder.

Essential: a non-destructive, predominantly non-epitheliotropic infiltrate of small mature lymphocytes confined to the gastrointestinal mucosa +/− submucosa; T lineage (CD4+, CD8+, CD4+/CD8+, or CD4−/CD8−), with TCRαβ expression; low proliferation index (Ki-67 < 10%).

Desirable: detection of clonal TR rearrangement (or somatic mutations) can assist in the distinction from an inflammatory disorder.

Staging is performed according to the Lugano classification, which has been adopted by the ninth-edition Union for International Cancer Control (UICC) TNM classification {25113753} [[Brierley JD, Giuliani M, O’Sullivan B, et al., editors. TNM Classification of Malignant Tumours. 9th ed. Oxford (UK): John Wiley & Sons; 2025. Bookref]].

Multiple sites in the GI tract are often involved, with chronic persistence of disease or a relapsing clinical course. Response to conventional chemotherapy is poor, but patients typically have prolonged survival with conservative management (e.g. steroid therapy). Disease progression with extragastrointestinal spread or transformation to aggressive lymphoma can occur, usually decades after diagnosis {10517900;23861889;29592893;29986618;31558678;36472661}.
